title: Implant Internal Image
description: An adversary implants malicious content into a container image stored in an internal registry the cluster pulls from. Once provisioning tools (GitOps controllers, Helm releases, deployment pipelines) deploy the latest tag of the affected image, the adversary gains persistent execution inside the cluster every time the workload restarts. Detection is anchored on registry write events, image digest divergence between policy and reality, and admission-time signature verification failures.

microsoft_k8s_matrix.name: Compromised Image In Registry
microsoft_k8s_matrix.description: An adversary places a backdoored image in the cluster's internal or third-party registry. Workloads pulling that image, often by a mutable tag like `latest` or `prod`, execute the implanted code on every restart. The Microsoft matrix categorizes this as Initial Access from the cluster's point of view; MITRE categorizes it as Persistence from the adversary's. The Microsoft matrix entry MS-TA9002 also cross-maps to T1195.002 (Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain), framing the same action as a supply-chain primitive.

data_components.name: Image Creation
data_components.definition: Construction of a container or VM image, including the principal that pushed it, the source build pipeline, the resulting digest, and the layers added relative to the previous tag of the same repository.
relevant_events: Registry push event with digest, repository, tag, and authenticated principal
Image build event from a CI system with provenance attestation (SLSA, in-toto)
Layer diff between consecutive pushes to the same tag

data_components.name: Image Modification
data_components.definition: Replacement of an existing tag's digest in a registry without a corresponding pipeline build event. The mismatch between expected provenance and observed digest is the highest-fidelity signal.
relevant_events: Registry tag-update event where the new digest does not match any digest produced by the canonical CI pipeline in the last N days
Sigstore/Cosign verification failure at admission time

data_components.name: Application Log Content
data_components.definition: Registry server access logs (Harbor, ECR, GCR, GHCR, ACR, Quay), Kubernetes admission webhook logs, and signature-verification controller logs. The push-side and pull-side stories live here.
relevant_events: Registry server log entry: PUT manifest by an unexpected principal
Kubernetes admission webhook denial: signature verification failed
Pull event correlated with a manifest pushed in the last 5 minutes

data_components.name: User Account Authentication
data_components.definition: Authentication events against the registry. A push from a stale or unexpected credential is a strong indicator of compromise even before the manifest is parsed.
relevant_events: Registry login by a service account that has not been used in 90 days
Registry login from a source IP outside the CI runner egress range
Token issued to a registry write role outside business hours

detection_strategies.name: Detection Strategy for T1525 Implant Internal Image
detection_strategies.summary: Compare every registry push and tag-mutation event against the set of digests produced by the canonical build pipeline. Surface any tag whose current digest has no matching CI provenance, and any pull of such a tag by a cluster workload.

detection_strategies.name: Container image backdoor followed by deployment
detection_strategies.summary: Malicious code injection into container images followed by a registry push and subsequent use in new pod deployments inside the cluster.

detection_strategies.name: Cloud VM image with persistence followed by provisioning
detection_strategies.summary: Creation or alteration of cloud VM images (AMIs, custom images) containing persistence mechanisms, followed by infrastructure provisioning using these compromised images.

vendor_detections.title: Registry tag mutated by a non-CI principal
vendor_detections.intent: Surface any registry manifest push that updates a tag in production-relevant namespaces when the principal is not a known CI runner identity.
required_telemetry: Wiz registry connector enabled for every registry the cluster pulls from (ECR, GCR, GHCR, ACR, Quay, Harbor)
ciIdentities and protectedRepoPrefix maintained as constants, not inlined per query
Audit logging enabled on the registry
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Manual operator pushes (break-glass, hotfix) appear here and are legitimate. Treat as alerts that page a maintainer for justification rather than auto-remediated.
vendor_detections.limitations: Cannot detect implants performed via legitimate CI access (insider threat, compromised CI). Pair with provenance verification (SLSA, in-toto) at admission.

vendor_detections.title: Provenance gap: deployed digest absent from CI build history
vendor_detections.intent: For every distinct image digest pulled by the cluster in the last 24 hours, confirm that digest appears in the CI build-attestation table. Anything that does not match is either a manual push or an implant.
vendor_detections.query:
-- K8S.PUBLIC.IMAGE_PULLS:    one row per pod-pulled image observation
-- CI.PUBLIC.BUILD_ATTESTATIONS: one row per CI-produced image with provenance
WITH recent_pulls AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    cluster_name,
    image_repository,
    image_tag,
    image_digest,
    MIN(event_time) AS first_seen
  FROM K8S.PUBLIC.IMAGE_PULLS
  WHERE event_time >= DATEADD(hour, -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
)
SELECT
  p.cluster_name,
  p.image_repository,
  p.image_tag,
  p.image_digest,
  p.first_seen
FROM        recent_pulls p
LEFT JOIN   CI.PUBLIC.BUILD_ATTESTATIONS a
     ON     a.image_repository = p.image_repository
        AND a.image_digest     = p.image_digest
WHERE       a.image_digest IS NULL
ORDER  BY   p.first_seen DESC;
required_telemetry: Image-pull events landed in K8S.PUBLIC.IMAGE_PULLS (e.g., from kubelet event hooks or admission controller logs)
CI build attestations landed in CI.PUBLIC.BUILD_ATTESTATIONS (Sigstore Rekor entries, in-toto attestations, or pipeline run artifacts)
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Vendored base images that the team pulls directly without a pipeline build will appear as gaps; allowlist their repositories explicitly.
vendor_detections.limitations: Lake latency means this is hunt/audit, not real-time prevention. Pair with admission-time signature verification (Cosign verify-attestation, Connaisseur, Kyverno verifyImages) for blocking.

vendor_detections.title: Falco: pull of an unsigned image at admission time
vendor_detections.intent: Fail closed on any pod that admits an image whose signature does not verify against the trusted Sigstore policy. Falco wires up Cosign verify-attestation through its image plugin.
vendor_detections.query:
- macro: trusted_signers
  condition: (image.signers.subject contains "https://github.com/example-org/.github/.github/workflows/build.yml")

- rule: Unsigned Or Untrusted Image Admitted
  desc: A pod is admitted with an image whose signature does not verify against the trusted policy.
  condition: kevt and pod and kcreate and not trusted_signers
  output: >
    Pod admitted with unsigned/untrusted image
    (user=%ka.user.name pod=%ka.target.name ns=%ka.target.namespace
     images=%ka.req.pod.images signers=%image.signers)
  priority: CRITICAL
  source: k8s_audit
  tags: [supply_chain, mitre_persistence, T1525]
required_telemetry: Falco with k8s_audit plugin and image-signature plugin enabled
Sigstore policy controller (or equivalent) invoked at admission so image.signers is populated
Trusted signer subjects maintained as a constant list, not literal strings inline
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: First rollout of a new pipeline often produces unsigned images; coordinate the policy turn-on with platform team.
vendor_detections.limitations: Requires upstream signing discipline. If only a fraction of images are signed, this alert fires constantly and is ignored.

mitre_cross_references.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
mitre_cross_references.rationale: T1525 covers implanting a malicious image inside the victim's own registry (internal persistence). T1195.002 covers poisoning a software artifact before it reaches the victim -- the distinction is where in the supply chain the compromise occurs. When a base image is tampered with upstream (public registry, CI/CD pipeline) and the victim's cluster pulls it, T1195.002 is the correct technique; T1525 applies when an authenticated attacker modifies an image already inside the victim's private registry. Defenders should alert on both pull-from-poisoned-upstream (T1195.002) and push-to-internal-registry (T1525) as separate but related event chains.

mitre_cross_references.name: Deploy Container
mitre_cross_references.rationale: The implanted image is operationalized when a new container is deployed from it (T1610). Atomic Red Team T1610 test documents this exact chain: adversary builds a malicious image then launches it via docker create/start or kubectl apply. Detection of image implantation alone (T1525) is incomplete without chaining to the first deploy event that activates the payload.
